disclaimer: Suggested clinical decision support reference only. Clinician must verify before ordering medication.

common_cold.name: Common Cold (Viral Rhinitis)
suggested_causes: Rhinovirus infection (~50%)
Seasonal coronavirus, adenovirus, or RSV
Upper airway mucosal inflammation
common_cold.common_remedies: Adequate oral hydration, rest, saline nasal rinse/spray, paracetamol 500-1000mg PRN for headache/malaise, first-generation antihistamines or decongestants if nasal congestion severe. Antibiotics NOT indicated.

influenza.name: Influenza (Seasonal Flu)
suggested_causes: Influenza A or B viral infection with systemic cytokine response
Respiratory droplet transmission during seasonal epidemic
influenza.common_remedies: Bed rest, oral fluids, paracetamol or ibuprofen for fever and myalgias. Consider oseltamivir (Tamiflu 75mg BD for 5 days) if within 48 hours of symptom onset or high-risk patient. Monitor for secondary bacterial pneumonia.

viral_fever.name: Acute Viral Pyrexia
suggested_causes: Self-limiting systemic viral infection (Enterovirus, Adenovirus, Parvovirus)
Non-specific viremia with endogenous pyrogen release
viral_fever.common_remedies: Symptomatic antipyretic therapy with paracetamol (650mg QDS PRN), liberal fluid intake (2-3 L/day), oral rehydration salts, tepid sponging if temp > 39°C. Re-evaluate if fever persists > 5 days.

dengue.name: Dengue Fever (Breakbone Fever)
suggested_causes: Dengue virus (DENV 1-4) transmission via Aedes aegypti / albopictus vector
Capillary fragility and immune-mediated thrombocytopenia
dengue.common_remedies: Strict oral rehydration therapy (ORS, fruit juices, electrolyte solutions). Paracetamol 500-650mg for pyrexia (DO NOT prescribe NSAIDs, aspirin, or corticosteroids due to hemorrhage risk). Daily CBC monitoring for hematocrit rise and platelet nadir.

typhoid.name: Typhoid Enteric Fever
suggested_causes: Salmonella enterica serovar Typhi / Paratyphi bacterial infection
Fecal-oral transmission via contaminated water or food
typhoid.common_remedies: Targeted antibiotic therapy: Azithromycin 1g/day oral x 7 days or IV Ceftriaxone 2g/day x 10-14 days based on local susceptibility. High-calorie bland diet, electrolyte repletion, monitor for intestinal perforation or GI bleed in 2nd-3rd week.

malaria.name: Malaria
suggested_causes: Plasmodium falciparum or P. vivax protozoan infection via Anopheles mosquito bite
Intraerythrocytic schizogony causing cyclical paroxysmal pyrexia
malaria.common_remedies: Artemisinin-based combination therapy (ACT, e.g. Artemether-Lumefantrine oral or IV Artesunate for severe/cerebral malaria). Primaquine for P. vivax radical cure after G6PD testing. Fluid management and glucose monitoring.

covid19.name: COVID-19 / Acute Respiratory Illness
suggested_causes: SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus infection with upper/lower respiratory inflammation
Aerosol transmission and host angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) binding
covid19.common_remedies: Home isolation, pulse oximetry tracking (target SpO2 >= 94%), hydration, antipyretics. If SpO2 < 94% or high risk: oral nirmatrelvir-ritonavir (Paxlovid) within 5 days, or dexamethasone 6mg/day if requiring supplemental oxygen.

gastroenteritis.name: Acute Gastroenteritis / Food Poisoning
suggested_causes: Viral gastroenteritis (Norovirus, Rotavirus)
Bacterial toxin (Staphylococcus aureus, Bacillus cereus, Campylobacter, Salmonella)
Dietary indiscretion or contaminated water intake
gastroenteritis.common_remedies: Aggressive oral rehydration with WHO-ORS formula (1-2 glasses per loose stool), zinc supplementation, probiotics. Avoid anti-motility agents (loperamide) in bloody/febrile diarrhea. Reserve antibiotics (ciprofloxacin or azithromycin) for severe dysentery.

uti.name: Urinary Tract Infection (Cystitis)
suggested_causes: Ascending bacterial colonization, primarily Uropathogenic E. coli (80%)
Klebsiella, Proteus mirabilis, or Enterococcus species
uti.common_remedies: Oral Nitrofurantoin 100mg BD x 5 days or Fosfomycin trometamol 3g single dose or Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (if local resistance < 20%). Increased water intake, urinary alkalinizers (potassium citrate) for dysuria relief. Urine culture if recurrent.

pneumonia.name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP)
suggested_causes: Streptococcus pneumoniae (pneumococcus)
Atypical pathogens (Mycoplasma pneumoniae, Chlamydia pneumoniae, Legionella)
Viral lower respiratory involvement (Influenza, RSV, SARS-CoV-2)
pneumonia.common_remedies: Outpatient: Amoxicillin 1g TDS oral + Azithromycin 500mg daily or Doxycycline. Inpatient / severe (CURB-65 >= 2): IV Ceftriaxone 2g daily + Macrolide, supplemental oxygen to maintain SpO2 >= 92%, chest physiotherapy.

bronchitis.name: Acute Bronchitis
suggested_causes: Viral tracheobronchial mucosal inflammation (>90%: Influenza, Parainfluenza, Coronavirus)
Airway hyperreactivity and post-infectious bronchial irritation
bronchitis.common_remedies: Supportive care, humidified air, honey/dextromethorphan for sleep-disturbing cough, inhaled salbutamol / albuterol bronchodilator if wheezing present. Antibiotics provide no proven clinical benefit in uncomplicated viral bronchitis.

asthma.name: Bronchial Asthma Exacerbation
suggested_causes: Reversible bronchospasm and eosinophilic airway inflammation
Triggered by viral respiratory infection, aeroallergens, cold air, or physical exertion
asthma.common_remedies: Inhaled short-acting beta-2 agonist (Salbutamol 4-8 puffs via spacer Q20min for 1 hour), short course oral corticosteroids (Prednisolone 40-50mg/day x 5 days), inhaled corticosteroid maintenance (ICS-Formoterol). Monitor peak expiratory flow.

hypertension.name: Essential Hypertension
suggested_causes: Primary essential systemic vascular resistance elevation
High dietary sodium, arterial stiffness, sympathetic overactivity, metabolic factors
hypertension.common_remedies: Lifestyle modification (DASH diet, sodium < 2g/day, weight management, aerobic exercise). Pharmacotherapy based on stage: ACE inhibitor / ARB (e.g. Telmisartan 40mg), Amlodipine 5mg, or Thiazide diuretic. Confirm home BP diary.

type2_diabetes.name: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus
suggested_causes: Peripheral insulin resistance combined with progressive pancreatic beta-cell secretory defect
Genetic predisposition compounded by adiposity and sedentary lifestyle
type2_diabetes.common_remedies: Lifestyle optimization (medical nutrition therapy, regular physical activity). First-line pharmacotherapy: Metformin 500mg-1000mg BD with meals. Add SGLT2 inhibitor (Empagliflozin) or GLP-1 RA if cardiorenal risk factors present. Target HbA1c < 7.0%.

anemia.name: Iron Deficiency / Nutritional Anemia
suggested_causes: Negative iron balance from chronic occult blood loss (GI, menorrhagia) or inadequate dietary intake
Impaired gastrointestinal absorption (celiac, atrophic gastritis)
anemia.common_remedies: Oral ferrous ascorbate or ferrous sulfate 100-200mg elemental iron daily on empty stomach with Vitamin C (avoid tea/calcium within 2 hours). Treat underlying cause of blood loss. Parenteral iron (ferric carboxymaltose) if intolerant or severe.

migraine.name: Migraine / Vascular Cephalea
suggested_causes: Trigeminovascular system activation with neurogenic dural inflammation and cortical spreading depression
Sensory hypersensitivity triggered by stress, sleep disruption, or dietary factors
migraine.common_remedies: Acute abortive therapy: Oral Triptan (Sumatriptan 50-100mg or Rizatriptan 10mg) taken early at onset + NSAID (Naproxen 500mg). Rest in dark, quiet room. If frequent (>4/month), initiate prophylaxis (Propranolol, Topiramate, or Amitriptyline).

allergic_rhinitis.name: Allergic Rhinitis (Hay Fever)
suggested_causes: IgE-mediated type I hypersensitivity reaction to airborne allergens (pollen, dust mites, mold, animal dander)
Nasal mucosal histamine and leukotriene degranulation
allergic_rhinitis.common_remedies: Intranasal corticosteroid spray (Fluticasone furoate or Mometasone 1-2 sprays/nostril daily - gold standard). Second-generation non-sedating oral antihistamine (Cetirizine 10mg, Fexofenadine 120mg). Saline nasal irrigation. Allergen avoidance.

heart_disease.name: Coronary Artery Disease (CAD)
suggested_causes: Atherosclerotic coronary artery plaque causing demand-supply myocardial ischemia
Risk factors: hypertension, dyslipidemia, diabetes, tobacco use, age, genetic predisposition
heart_disease.common_remedies: Immediate antiplatelet therapy (Aspirin 75-100mg daily), high-intensity statin (Atorvastatin 40-80mg), sublingual nitroglycerin PRN for angina, beta-blocker (Metoprolol succinate). Prompt cardiology evaluation, 12-lead ECG, troponin, and coronary angiography.
